Hi Samir / Jenna — great to meet you both. Quick recap and next steps from our side based on your questions: 

1) SOC 2: Redwood is currently in SOC 2 Type II readiness; control implementation and audits are on track. We expect Type II completion by end of Q1 2027. I'll attach the readiness summary.

2) GDPR / HIPAA: we support a standard DPA for EU customers and offer a BAA for customers requiring HIPAA coverage on enterprise contracts/Private deployments. We can share the DPA/BAA templates once we progress to procurement.

3) Audit logs (what we capture):
   - Admin activity (user creation, role changes, policy edits)
   - Authentication events (SSO/JWT, failed/successful logins)
   - API request logs (request ID, endpoint, method, response code, latency)
   - Inference-level metadata (model id, prompt metadata, token counts) — note: full prompt/response bodies are not retained by default for hosted plans unless enabled; we can discuss scope
   - System events (service restarts, deployment rollouts, autoscaling actions)

4) Exportability & integration:
   - Exports: CSV/JSON exports and daily/near-real-time delivery to customer-owned S3 buckets (supporting S3 object lock for immutability on the customer's side)
   - Streaming: we can stream logs to a customer SIEM via syslog/HTTPS/Kafka connectors or integrate with CloudWatch/Stackdriver depending on region

5) Immutability & retention:
   - For Dedicated/Private customers we support write-once exports and can configure S3 Object Lock/retention settings. For hosted customers we provide signed export manifests and can retain immutable snapshots on request as part of an enterprise package

6) PII / redaction: request/response bodies are treated as sensitive; we offer configurable redaction/scrubbing and tokenization options and can apply retention policies per workload.

Attachments: redwood-audit-logging-overview.pdf, redwood-soc2-readiness-202611.pdf (stubs)

Next steps: 
- Aditya (cc'ed) can run a 45-min technical deep-dive with your infra/security team to walk through a sample log schema and set up a streaming demo.
- Evelyn (cc'ed) can kick off the vendor security questionnaire if you'd like to share it (or we can send ours).

Please let me know 2–3 times that work for next week and whether you prefer S3 export or streaming for the initial integration.

Thanks,

Hi Samir / Jenna — adding a few technical details to Marissa's summary that often help during the security review: 

- Log schema: each log record includes timestamp, event_type, user_id (internal), actor_ip, request_id (uuid), service, endpoint, status_code, latency_ms, model_id, token_count, and optional metadata. Sample schema attached in the follow-up deck.
- Inference payloads: for hosted customers we do not persist full prompt/response content by default; customers can opt-in to retain inference payloads for X days for debugging/obs. For enterprise/private deployments we can support configurable retention windows and redaction rules.
- Encryption: all logs are encrypted at rest with AES-256; keys are managed via customer-managed KMS for Private deployments and by Redwood KMS for hosted. We support HSM-backed key storage for enterprises requiring FIPS/HSM.
- Immutability: we support exporting daily signed archives (SHA256 manifest) to customer S3 with optional object lock to enforce immutability on the bucket side. For Dedicated customers we can implement write-once retention policies inside the cluster export pipeline.
- SIEM integration: we have connectors for Splunk/Datadog/SumoLogic and a generic syslog/HTTPS forwarder; Kafka export available for high-throughput setups.

Happy to share a sample log file prior to the call. If you prefer S3 exports we can provision a temporary bucket and drop a 48-hour sample.

—Aditya
